ChAI-Net learns a regulatory code for chromatin co-accessibility.

ChAI-Net is a deep learning model trained on single-molecule long-read footprinting data from mouse embryonic stem cells to learn how transcription factor binding and nucleosome positioning are coordinated within cis-regulatory elements. The model captures a regulatory code governing chromatin co-accessibility, revealing coordinated protein-DNA interactions that bulk methods obscure.

Microbiome science needs AI competence, not just AI literacy.

The authors argue that microbiome researchers need deeper AI competence—not just basic literacy—because common pitfalls like data leakage, incomplete metadata, ecological confounding, and unverified generative-AI outputs can yield convincing but biologically misleading conclusions. They propose a five-capability AI-competence framework covering data and platform fluency, machine-learning competency, and related skills to guide training in the field.

Viral host assignment across the tree of life with VHAMSTeR.

VHAMSTeR is a new classification framework that predicts the host of viral sequences across five broad categories (prokaryote, animal, plant, fungi, protist) by combining fine-tuned genomic language model embeddings with explicit biological features such as genome architecture and protein homology. It substantially outperforms existing host prediction methods, achieving MCC > 0.91 for DNA viruses and > 0.69 for RNA viruses. This addresses the widespread problem of viruses lacking known hosts across the tree of life.

De novo Design of a Vanadium Haloperoxidase.

This preprint reports the de novo design of a vanadium-dependent haloperoxidase, an enzyme that catalyzes carbon-halogen bond formation using a vanadate cofactor. The key challenge was that vanadate is an anionic oxometalate requiring precise hydrogen-bonding and electrostatic networks rather than the coordinate-covalent bonds typical for metal-binding proteins. The work demonstrates that computational protein design can be extended to this unusual cofactor-binding mode, opening a route to engineered halogenases.

LongVerse: verified AI agents for Nanopore and PacBio DNA methylation analysis.

LongVerse is an AI-agent system that converts a single English instruction into haplotype-resolved DNA methylation calls from Nanopore or PacBio reads, with agents configuring a pinned pipeline rather than writing code. On the HG002 reference genome, agent and human expert outputs were byte-identical (r = 1.000) and concordant with bisulfite sequencing (r = 0.943 and 0.884), at a cost of $0.12–$0.54 per run. The work demonstrates that agent outputs can be validated against an independent measurement rather than only rubric or LLM-judge checks.
